newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil aims to release draft of CVRD bid specs Fri.
newsitem.headline: Brazil aims to release draft of CVRD bid specs Fri.

text.p: Brazil aims to release a draft of the tender documents for the selloff of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) Friday, said BNDES president Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros.
Mendonca de Barros also said the draft will not include Vale's base price and the auction date for the sale of a 40-45 percent voting stake in the firm.
However, Mendonca de Barros said BNDES will propose a minimum price and an auction date when it presents the draft to the National Privatization Council (CND) at its next meeting on March 5.
"The draft will not include the minimum price and the auction date. We will suggest them separately," he told reporters.
Vale's base price and auction date proposals also will be submitted to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso following a normal procedure in Brazil's privatizations.
On Monday, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir had said the federal government could publish the bid specifications for Vale's sale as early as Friday.
Vale's privatization is expected to begin in April.

Speaking at a seminar on private savings, Mendonca de Barros said Brazil's privatization revenues are expected to hit $10 billion in 1997 with the sale of CVRD, state power utilities Coelba, Cemat, Energipe, Cosern and Enersul, and the federal government's remaining stake in Light.
He also said he expects Furnas and Eletrosul, subsidiaries of federal Eletrobras, to be only privatized early next year and not at the end of 1997 as the market has been speculating.

Regarding the privatization of federal Telebras system, he said he expects Sao Paulo state telecom unit Telesp and long-distance unit Embratel to be the first subsidiaries to be auctioned off, but he did not say when.
